title: Spend the view’s one red on the point the title names.
rule: Rule 05.3 gives each view one working red and says which job claims it first. In a chart, the red goes to the one point, bar or line the title names, inside the 1 px Charcoal keyline of Rule 05.5, and that mark carries its own label. Every other mark keeps the subject and context inks of Rule 05.7.

When an error or a step the reader can take already holds the view’s red, the named point gives it up and takes Charcoal at the subject weight, with its label. Red never codes a series, a group or a step on a scale.

text: One red mark tells a reader where to look first, and the title tells them why. A second red mark splits their attention, and red that codes a group reads as a warning about that group.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: Name the one point in the spec (labels.named for the subject ink); the kit counts working reds and fails a view with two.

correct.caption: The title names the Ninth Circuit, and its bar alone takes the view’s red, inside its keyline, with every other court in gray.
correct.alt: Bars of active judges on the 13 federal courts of appeals, the Ninth Circuit’s 29 in red with a dark edge and the rest in gray, from 17 on the Fifth Circuit down to 6 on the First Circuit.
correct.notes: Drawn here from the directory's rows, counted by script, until the kit takes a red point by name (request ED-E1).

failure.caption: Fails Rule 14.6. Red falls on three courts while the title names one, so a reader cannot tell which bar the title means.
failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. The same bars with three courts in red, the Ninth, Fifth and Sixth Circuits, under a title that names one.
